feed.title: India's Growing Crude Influence; Analog Devices' AI Strategy; and the Evolving Media Landscape
feed.summary: This S&P Global update covers India's increasing influence in global crude markets due to its diversified sourcing and refining capabilities, as highlighted at APPEC. It also discusses Analog Devices' acquisition of Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion to expand its AI footprint, forecasting significant revenue growth driven by industrial and communications demand. Furthermore, the article touches on trends reshaping global media, including streaming profitability, the enduring value of live sports, and the impact of 5G and fiber network expansions, as explored in the "MediaTalk" podcast.

feed.title: Altria Group Inc's Dividend Analysis
feed.summary: Altria Group Inc. (NYSE: MO) recently announced a $1.11 per share dividend, with an ex-dividend date of September 15, 2026. The company boasts a long history of dividend payments and increases, earning it the status of a "dividend king." While its dividend yield is attractive, investors should consider the high payout ratio of 0.77 and moderate growth rates in revenue, EPS, and EBITDA when assessing the dividend's long-term sustainability amidst industry challenges.

feed.title: Costco launching 14 warehouses in next 2 months
feed.summary: Costco is planning to open 14 new warehouses in the next two months, including four in Canada in November, with some locations replacing older, smaller stores. This expansion aligns with Costco's long-term strategy to open 30 or more locations within the next five to ten years. The news follows strong financial performance for Costco, with August net sales increasing by 9.9% to $23.7 billion and July net sales rising by 10.7%.

feed.title: Merck & Co Inc's Dividend Analysis
feed.summary: Merck & Co Inc (NYSE: MRK) recently declared a $0.85 per share dividend, maintaining its long-standing history of consistent payouts and dividend growth, making it a dividend aristocrat. While the company demonstrates strong profitability and growth metrics, its current payout ratio of 1.05 raises concerns about the near-term sustainability of its dividend. Investors should closely monitor future payout ratios and growth trends to assess the reliability of its dividend growth streak.

feed.title: Lam Research Vs. Applied Materials: Who Actually Helps ASML Share Prices Rise Higher?
feed.summary: This article compares Lam Research and Applied Materials, both major players in the semiconductor equipment industry, to determine which one is a better proxy for ASML's share price performance. While both companies are benefiting from increased AI capital expenditure, Lam Research's specialized etch tools are argued to have a more direct correlation with ASML's high-margin EUV systems due to the one-for-one scaling of etch layers with EUV patterning. Applied Materials offers a more diversified portfolio and a lower P/E, making it a safer, diversified compounder, but Lam is presented as the cleaner instrument for direct correlation to ASML's EUV cycle.

feed.title: MMSD nears decision on $700M wastewater contract as lawsuit awaits ruling
feed.summary: The Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District (MMSD) is close to awarding a 10-year, $700 million wastewater operations contract amidst a lawsuit filed by the incumbent operator, Veolia North America. A judge has allowed the bidding process to continue but prevented MMSD from signing a final agreement until the lawsuit is resolved. The decision process has been complicated by accusations against Veolia and questions surrounding the challenger, Jacobs Solutions, particularly regarding its past ties to Palantir and union relations.

feed.title: The sustainability risks threatening AI’s resilience narrative
feed.summary: This report from S&P Global explores the sustainability challenges facing the rapid expansion of AI, focusing on three key areas: lagging corporate AI governance, increasing pressure on energy systems from data centers, and growing community resistance to data center construction in the US. Despite significant investments in AI, over half of surveyed firms lack robust AI governance, exposing them to risks. The immense electricity demands of data centers are complicating decarbonization efforts and leading to increased fossil fuel use, while local communities are pushing back against data center development due to concerns about resource consumption, noise, and environmental impact, leading to project delays and cancellations.

feed.title: Rollins Inc. stock recovers from 1-year low as analysts see upside
feed.summary: Rollins Inc. stock closed at USD 35.30 on September 14, 2026, recovering from a 12-month low but remaining significantly below the consensus analyst price target of USD 48.71, implying a 38.0% upside. Despite a year-to-date decline of 41.2%, the company reported a 7.9% year-over-year revenue increase in Q2 2026, though EPS slightly missed estimates. Analysts maintain a "Hold" rating, acknowledging the company's quality but noting its premium valuation and the need for continued strong financial performance.

feed.title: Celebrity Cruises floats first river ship for planned 20-vessel fleet
feed.summary: Celebrity Cruises has floated out its first river cruise ship, the 135-meter Celebrity Compass, in Rotterdam, marking a significant milestone for its planned entry into European river cruising in August 2027. Royal Caribbean Group intends to develop a 20-vessel European river fleet by 2031, with the first season selling out rapidly. The Celebrity Compass will operate on the Danube, accommodating 170 passengers in 86 staterooms with various premium features.

feed.title: KKR pays €528m for 49% stake in Realty Income European venture
feed.summary: KKR has acquired a 49% stake for €528m in a new European joint venture with Realty Income. The venture is seeded with a 54-property net-lease portfolio across Spain, Ireland, Poland, and the Netherlands. Realty Income will retain a 51% majority interest and continue to manage the assets, expanding its private capital strategy into Europe.

feed.title: Kraft Heinz bets on more flavors for Philadelphia cream cheese as it looks to revive brands
feed.summary: Kraft Heinz is launching new Philadelphia cream cheese flavors, including Mike's Hot Honey, salted caramel, and cranberry orange, as part of a strategy to revitalize its iconic brands. The company is investing $700 million into its business, with a significant portion going towards Philadelphia cream cheese, to create excitement in the category and regain market share. This move comes after years of disappointing sales and a paused plan to break up the company.

feed.title: AI Stocks Fell, but Workday and Adobe Jumped. A Favorite AI Disruption Trade Just Flinched
feed.summary: Workday (WDAY) and Adobe (ADBE) stock prices rose after calls to slow down frontier AI development, in contrast to the broader AI stock market which saw declines. This shift suggests that established software platforms might have more time to integrate AI as a feature, rather than being disrupted by new AI models. Both companies showed strong AI adoption in their recent earnings reports, although long-term growth and market skepticism remain factors.

feed.title: Trump's Marijuana Rescheduling Push Is Back in Focus. Is Tilray Stock Finally a Buy?
feed.summary: The article discusses the renewed focus on President Trump's push to reschedule marijuana to Schedule III, a move that could significantly impact companies like Tilray Brands (NASDAQ: TLRY). While rescheduling wouldn't federally legalize recreational cannabis, it would ease research and expand medical marijuana opportunities, areas where Tilray already has a strong international presence. The author suggests that Tilray's improved financial standing makes it a more compelling investment now, even if broader federal reform faces further delays or never fully materializes.

feed.title: Citizens reiterates KKR Real Estate Financial Trust stock rating

feed.title: Jim Cramer Says Lululemon (LULU) is in “No Man’s Land” After Another Brutal Quarter

feed.title: Realty Income targets European data centres after $6bn deal
feed.summary: Realty Income, a US-based net-lease giant, is expanding its focus to European data centers, eyeing markets like Frankfurt, London, Paris, and Barcelona, to capitalize on growing digital infrastructure demand. This expansion follows a $6bn deal in the US and aims to replicate its successful net-lease strategy in Europe, targeting single-tenant facilities with long-duration leases. The company sees attractive risk-adjusted opportunities in Europe due to less competition and a fragmented real estate market, further bolstered by a recent joint venture with KKR for European net-lease assets.

feed.title: Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) Sets $60 Billion Ceiling With Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM) As Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) Cuts Modem Ties
feed.summary: Amazon has set a potential $60 billion commercial relationship with Qualcomm for AI infrastructure, including server chips, systems, and optical connectivity. This agreement is significant for Qualcomm as Apple shifts its modem development in-house, impacting Qualcomm's revenue. The deal includes warrants for Amazon, vesting based on purchasing milestones, and aims to help Qualcomm diversify its revenue streams into data centers.

feed.title: Wells Fargo sees AI slowdown as unlikely despite safety calls
feed.summary: Wells Fargo believes a coordinated slowdown in AI development is improbable despite calls for safety pauses from industry leaders like Anthropic and OpenAI. The bank suggests that any slowdown is more likely to stem from supply-side bottlenecks such as power availability and permit delays, rather than a consensual halt in demand within the highly competitive AI market. Wells Fargo also noted that an elongated AI buildout due to these constraints could ultimately support long-term multiples for certain midstream companies.
